title: Catalog-based role binding and scope resolution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a catalog-driven RBAC v2 role binding service that resolves role scopes against the resource hierarchy and emits high-fidelity audit events suitable for downstream compliance and alerting. This ticket formalizes the data model for role bindings, the scope resolution algorithm (catalog + path-anchored scopes), permission matrix shape, audit schema, and SSO/SAML group-to-role mapping patterns. Goal: unblock implementation team building the resolver and contract for console + API enforcement.
design_decisions: Primary source of truth: resource catalog (immutable node IDs + typed parents). Role bindings reference catalog node IDs and positional scope descriptors (prefix / exact / subtree).

Permission checks are evaluated by a resolver that first computes effective scope (intersection of subject bindings and request resource path), then applies permission grants/denies ordered by specificity (exact > prefix > global).
Use positive grants + explicit denies model to allow narrow safety-critical overrides. Denies are rare and require security_review_required flag set to true for the binding.
Bindings support 'delegated' flag for temporary delegation (TTL-backed) to support admin delegation use-cases and just-in-time elevation patterns.

Audit events use a structured schema (flat key/value fields) to keep downstream ingestion simple: event_type, actor_id, subject_role, binding_id, resource_id, action, result, reason, request_id, trace_id, timestamp.

SSO/SAML integration: perform group-to-role assignment during SAML assertion processing (SCIM optional). Group membership stamped into OIDC token as roles_claim; role resolution occurs server-side to avoid token bloat.
tradeoffs: Catalog-first model requires a migration of existing freeform resource strings; tradeoff: more upfront work to canonicalize resources vs. more reliable scope resolution and efficient deny semantics.
Explicit denies add complexity to policy evaluation and potential for surprising blockages; mitigated by requiring security_review_required and audit trail for deny creation.
Storing bindings by catalog ID increases durability but makes cross-tenant imports harder; plan to support an import flow that maps external IDs to local catalog IDs.

Evaluating specific > prefix > global simplifies reasoning but may penalize performance for very deep hierarchies; we will cache resolved scope fragments per request_id for repeated checks in a single operation.
permissions_matrix_summary: Canonical permission matrix defined as rows of (resource_type, action, permission_code). Examples: 'model:read' allows GET on /models/:id and list on /models; 'runtime:invoke' maps to the token-level call/stream endpoints; 'billing:admin' maps to invoice/export consoles. Matrix is stored as normalized table in auth DB and referenced by role definitions; roles store a list of permission_codes and an optional parameterized constraint (e.g., max_rate_per_minute).
implementation_plan: 1) Schema: add tables: catalog_nodes (id, type, parent_id, path), role_definitions (id, name, permission_codes), role_bindings (id, role_id, subject_type, subject_id, scope_descriptor, delegated, ttl, created_by, security_review_required), denies (id, binding_id, reason).

2) Resolver service: HTTP service with endpoints /resolve-permissions and /explain-resolution returning effective grants and deny explanations. Implement caching layer keyed by (subject_id, resource_id, role_version).
3) API hooks: Enforce resolver in API gateway for control-plane operations and expose lightweight SDK for internal services to call resolver.
4) Console integration: admin UI to create role bindings with scope visualizer and a simulator that shows effective permissions for a chosen resource and subject.
5) Audit: emit structured events to centralized events pipeline and link binding creation/changes to change-log entries visible in Audit UI.
migration_path: Phase A (read-only): Ingest existing freeform resource strings into catalog_nodes as synthetic nodes; introduce mappings table old_string -> catalog_id.
Phase B (dual-write): New bindings created against catalog IDs; API layer accepts old string forms and maps them to catalog IDs using mappings table.
Phase C (cutover): Convert legacy bindings to catalog-based bindings during a background job; run reconciliation reports and surface mismatches to owners.
Phase D (cleanup): Remove legacy mapping endpoints after a stabilization period and mark migration done in infra metadata.
audit_integration: Emit events for binding lifecycle: binding.created, binding.updated, binding.deleted, binding.approved (if security_review_required), binding.expired.
Access check events: authz.check with fields [actor_id, subject_role_ids, resource_id, action, result(allow/deny), decision_reasons(array), resolver_version, request_id].
Retention and export: default 1 year retention for authz events (configurable per org), with exporter to S3 for compliance exports on-demand.
Alerting: large-scale deny storms (spike in denies for a single role or resource) should trigger paging to security oncall.
sso_saml_admin_controls: During SAML assertion, map incoming groups to role_binding creations via an ingestion job with an owner review step for new mappings (prevent silent elevation).
Support SCIM provisioning for orgs that require automated group sync; provisioning is rate-limited and logged as binding.created events.
Admin console: show 'source' column for bindings (manually created, SSO-mapped, SCIM-provisioned) and allow owners to require MFA or session duration constraints per binding.
Allow tenant-level policy to disable automatic group-to-role assignments (enforced by resolver).
qa_plan: Unit tests: resolver evaluation semantics (specificity ordering, deny precedence, delegated TTL), permission matrix lookups.
Integration tests: end-to-end checks via API gateway for common flows: model read, runtime invoke, console billing access.
Fuzz tests: generate random hierarchies + bindings to assert determinism and no N+1 lookups under 1000 simulated checks.
Security tests: verify deny lifecycle protections and that creating a deny requires security_review_required flag and triggers audit events.
rollout_plan: Canary: enable resolver for <10% of org traffic (internal orgs first) and run in parallel with legacy checker returning compare metrics for 2 weeks.
Fallback: gateway supports a fast-fail mode to fallback to legacy checker on high latency or errors from resolver.
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks, with automated reconciliation reports and weekly review meetings.
Post-launch: run a 30-day audit to validate that no critical workflows were affected and tune cache TTLs based on observed latency.
